title: [BUG] Claude Code frequently loses track of which directory it is in
body:
Claude Code frequently assumes it is in a different directory than the one it is in. A command will fail, and sometimes it takes several rounds of its own troubleshooting before it realizes the problem and changes to the correct directory. This is not only annoying, it's dangerous -- it caused me to lose 60 hours of wrangling with Claude Code when a git hard reset was executed in the wrong directory (#1668).

Please prepend to every prompt something like "You are currently in this working directory: ..." or whatever is necessary to get it to understand where it is starting from.
author: lukehutch

top_comments.author: cheeseblubber
top_comments.body: I have seen this issue as well. My folder structure is /Users/username/workspace/project-name claude code will often try to run code in workspace folder. I even moved to /Users/username/project-name outside of workspace folder but it seem to remember that folder and keeps navigating back to it.

top_comments.author: jxstanford
top_comments.body: I can't stress enough how significant this issue is. It's in the top 3 time wasters along with forgetting to source a venv  and not sufficiently testing code before marking a todo complete.

top_comments.author: lukehutch
top_comments.body: Right, it wastes both user time, but also user tokens (we're paying for this).
